Definition and constitutional example: A mark with neither intention nor addressee — e.g. the historical vestige of an unrecorded pact.
A trace preserved and retrievable — e.g. the minutes of a constituent assembly; the memorized but not yet applied teaching.
A record endowed with normative value; it creates obligations — e.g. a statute, a treaty, a judicial precedent.

An inscription that founds the system and on which all others depend — enacted (a supreme constitution), revealed (Qur'an and Sunna under the Saudi Basic Law), or distributed (the UK order; Israel's Basic Laws; the chthonic Dreaming).
